51	def _stage_name(stage_id: int) -> str:
52	    try:

54	    except ValueError:
55	        return f"stage_{stage_id:#04x}"

58	def _format_drop(rec: Drop, baseline: Drop | None) -> str:
59	    if baseline is None:
60	        return (
61	            f"DROP       state={rec.dropped_state} patch={rec.dropped_patch} "
62	            f"sink_bytes={rec.dropped_sink}  (baseline)"
63	        )
64	    return (
65	        f"DROP       "
66	        f"state={rec.dropped_state} (Δ{rec.dropped_state - baseline.dropped_state:+d})  "
67	        f"patch={rec.dropped_patch} (Δ{rec.dropped_patch - baseline.dropped_patch:+d})  "
68	        f"sink_bytes={rec.dropped_sink} (Δ{rec.dropped_sink - baseline.dropped_sink:+d})"
69	    )

72	class _DropBaseline:
73	    """Tracks the first DROP seen so subsequent ones print as session deltas."""
74	
75	    def __init__(self) -> None:
76	        self.first: Drop | None = None
77	
78	    def format(self, rec: Drop) -> str:
79	        line = _format_drop(rec, self.first)
80	        if self.first is None:
81	            self.first = rec
82	        return line

85	def _format_record(rec: Record, *, drop_baseline: _DropBaseline | None = None) -> str:
86	    epoch = getattr(rec.hdr, "frame_epoch", 0)
87	    ts = getattr(rec.hdr, "ts_counter", 0)
88	    if isinstance(rec, Session):
89	        return (
90	            f"SESSION    timer={rec.timer_freq_hz} Hz schema=v{rec.schema_version} "
91	            f"git={rec.fw_git_short:#010x}"
92	        )
93	    if isinstance(rec, Stamp):
94	        return (
95	            f"STAMP      epoch={epoch:>8} ts={ts:>12} "
96	            f"stage={_stage_name(rec.stage_id):<19} aux={rec.aux:#010x}"
97	        )
98	    if isinstance(rec, Detector):
99	        return (
100	            f"DETECTOR   epoch={epoch:>8} ts={ts:>12} "
101	            f"hold={rec.hold_dist} edge={rec.edge_dist} "
102	            f"P={rec.pressed_mask:#04x} E={rec.edge_active_mask:#04x}"
103	        )
104	    if isinstance(rec, Timing):
105	        return (
106	            f"TIMING     epoch={epoch:>8} ts={ts:>12} "
107	            f"pub={rec.publish_mask:#04x} cw={rec.chord_window_fill} "
108	            f"fifo={rec.fifo_depth} dir={rec.strum_dir}"
109	        )
110	    if isinstance(rec, Drop):
111	        return (
112	            drop_baseline.format(rec)
113	            if drop_baseline is not None
114	            else _format_drop(rec, None)
115	        )
116	    if isinstance(rec, TaskHighwater):
117	        try:
118	            name = TaskId(rec.task_id).name
119	        except ValueError:
120	            name = f"task_{rec.task_id}"
121	        return f"HWM        task={name:<16} words_free={rec.words}"
122	    if isinstance(rec, Patch):
123	        return f"PATCH      epoch={epoch:>8} {rec.frame_w}×{rec.frame_h}  (5 frets, 75 B BGR each)"
124	    if isinstance(rec, UnknownRecord):
125	        return f"UNKNOWN    type={rec.hdr.type:#04x} ({len(rec.raw)} B)"
126	    return repr(rec)

132	def cmd_live(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
133	    stats = FrameStats()
134	    record_count = 0
135	    last_status = time.monotonic()
136	    drop_records = 0
137	
138	    serial_src = SerialSource(args.port)
139	    if args.also_record:
140	        with serial_src as ser, TeeSource(ser, args.also_record) as tee:
141	            return _live_loop(_decode_stream(tee, stats), stats)
142	    else:
143	        with serial_src as ser:
144	            return _live_loop(_decode_stream(ser, stats), stats)
145	
146	
147	def _live_loop(records: Iterator[Record], stats: FrameStats) -> int:
148	    last_status = time.monotonic()
149	    record_count = 0
150	    drop_records = 0
151	    drop_baseline = _DropBaseline()
152	    for rec in records:
153	        record_count += 1
154	        if isinstance(rec, Drop):
155	            drop_records += 1
156	        print(_format_record(rec, drop_baseline=drop_baseline))
157	        now = time.monotonic()
158	        if (now - last_status) >= 1.0:
159	            print(
160	                f"  [status] frames={stats.frames_ok} resync_drop={stats.bytes_resync_dropped} "
161	                f"crc_err={stats.crc_mismatches} drop_recs={drop_records}",
162	                file=sys.stderr,
163	                flush=True,
164	            )
165	            last_status = now
166	    return 0

169	def cmd_record(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
170	    """Pure pass-through to disk; no decode."""
171	    out = Path(args.out)
172	    bytes_written = 0
173	    last_status = time.monotonic()
174	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser, out.open("wb") as fh:
175	        try:
176	            for chunk in ser:
177	                fh.write(chunk)
178	                fh.flush()
179	                bytes_written += len(chunk)
180	                now = time.monotonic()
181	                if (now - last_status) >= 1.0:
182	                    print(
183	                        f"recording {out.name}: {bytes_written} B",
184	                        file=sys.stderr,
185	                        flush=True,
186	                    )
187	                    last_status = now
188	        except KeyboardInterrupt:
189	            print(f"\nstopped after {bytes_written} B", file=sys.stderr)
190	    return 0

193	def cmd_decode(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
194	    stats = FrameStats()
195	    drop_baseline = _DropBaseline()
196	    with FileSource(args.path) as src:
197	        for rec in _decode_stream(src, stats):
198	            print(_format_record(rec, drop_baseline=drop_baseline))
199	    print(
200	        f"\n[decode] frames_ok={stats.frames_ok} resync_drop={stats.bytes_resync_dropped} "
201	        f"crc_err={stats.crc_mismatches} bad_len={stats.bad_lengths}",
202	        file=sys.stderr,
203	    )
204	    return 0

207	def cmd_summarize(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
208	    stats = FrameStats()
209	    records: list[Record] = []
210	    with FileSource(args.path) as src:
211	        records.extend(_decode_stream(src, stats))
212	
213	    session = find_session(records)
214	    try:
215	        check_schema(session)
216	    except SchemaVersionMismatch as e:
217	        print(f"FATAL: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
218	        return 2
219	
220	    timer_freq_hz = session.timer_freq_hz if session else 0
221	
222	    print("=== marvin perf-log summary ===")
223	    print(f"file: {args.path}")
224	    print(f"frames_ok={stats.frames_ok}  bytes_resync_dropped={stats.bytes_resync_dropped}  "
225	          f"crc_err={stats.crc_mismatches}  bad_len={stats.bad_lengths}")
226	    print(f"records: {len(records)}")
227	
228	    if session is None:
229	        print("(no SESSION record found — capture began mid-stream)")
230	    else:
231	        print(
232	            f"session: timer={session.timer_freq_hz} Hz  schema=v{session.schema_version}  "
233	            f"git={session.fw_git_short:#010x}"
234	        )
235	
236	    # Record-type histogram.
237	    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
238	    for rec in records:
239	        name = type(rec).__name__
240	        counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + 1
241	    print("\n--- record-type counts ---")
242	    for name in sorted(counts):
243	        print(f"  {name:<14} {counts[name]}")
244	
245	    # Latency.
246	    print("\n--- latency (µs) ---")
247	    if timer_freq_hz <= 0:
248	        print("  (skipped — no SESSION; cannot convert ts_counter to µs)")
249	    else:
250	        hists = compute_latencies(records, timer_freq_hz)
251	        print(f"  {'pair':<40} {'n':>6} {'p50':>10} {'p95':>10} {'p99':>10} {'max':>10}")
252	        for h in hists:
253	            a, b = h.pair
254	            label = f"{a.name} → {b.name}"
255	            if h.n == 0:
256	                print(f"  {label:<40} {0:>6} {'—':>10} {'—':>10} {'—':>10} {'—':>10}")
257	            else:
258	                print(
259	                    f"  {label:<40} {h.n:>6} {h.p50:>10.1f} {h.p95:>10.1f} "
260	                    f"{h.p99:>10.1f} {h.max:>10.1f}"
261	                )
262	
263	    # Drops.
264	    drops = compute_drops(records)
265	    print("\n--- drops (since-session / cumulative since boot) ---")
266	    print(
267	        f"  state:      Δ{drops.since_session_state} records  "
268	        f"(cum {drops.final_state}, max step {drops.max_state_delta})"
269	    )
270	    print(
271	        f"  patch:      Δ{drops.since_session_patch} records  "
272	        f"(cum {drops.final_patch}, max step {drops.max_patch_delta})"
273	    )
274	    print(
275	        f"  sink_bytes: Δ{drops.since_session_sink_bytes} bytes  "
276	        f"(cum {drops.final_sink_bytes}, max step {drops.max_sink_bytes_delta})"
277	    )
278	    print(f"  drop records observed: {drops.n_drop_records}")
279	
280	    # HWM.
281	    hwm = compute_hwm(records)
282	    if hwm:
283	        print("\n--- stack high-water (StackType_t words free) ---")
284	        for series in sorted(hwm.values(), key=lambda s: s.task_id):
285	            samples = series.samples
286	            print(
287	                f"  {series.task_name:<16}  n={len(samples):>4}  "
288	                f"min={series.min_words}  last={samples[-1][1] if samples else '—'}"
289	            )
290	
291	    # Warnings.
292	    warns = check_frame_epoch_monotonic(records) + check_video_publish_cadence(
293	        records, timer_freq_hz
294	    )
295	    if warns:
296	        print("\n--- warnings ---")
297	        for w in warns[:50]:
298	            print(f"  [{w.kind}] {w.message}")
299	        if len(warns) > 50:
300	            print(f"  …and {len(warns) - 50} more")
301	    return 0

306	
307	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
308	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
309	        prog="marvin-perf",
310	        description="Decode and analyze marvin firmware perf-log streams.",
311	    )
312	    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

1	"""Byte sources feeding `framing.iter_frames`.
2	
3	Each source is an iterable of `bytes` chunks. Chunk size is not load-bearing —
4	the framer handles arbitrary boundaries.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
10	from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
11	from pathlib import Path
12	from typing import BinaryIO
13	
14	
15	# ─── File source ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
16	
17	
18	class FileSource(AbstractContextManager["FileSource"]):
19	    """Iterate over fixed-size chunks from a captured `.bin` file."""
20	
21	    def __init__(self, path: str | Path, chunk_bytes: int = 64 * 1024) -> None:
22	        self.path = Path(path)
23	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
24	        self._fh: BinaryIO | None = None
25	
26	    def __enter__(self) -> "FileSource":
27	        self._fh = self.path.open("rb")
28	        return self
29	
30	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
31	        if self._fh is not None:
32	            self._fh.close()
33	            self._fh = None
34	
35	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
36	        if self._fh is None:
37	            raise RuntimeError("FileSource must be used as a context manager")
38	        while True:
39	            chunk = self._fh.read(self.chunk_bytes)
40	            if not chunk:
41	                return
42	            yield chunk
43	
44	
45	# ─── Serial source ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
46	
47	
48	class SerialSource(AbstractContextManager["SerialSource"]):
49	    """Read bytes from the marvin USB-device CDC ACM port via pyserial.
50	
51	    The firmware sink is DTR-gated (`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:216`); pyserial raises
52	    DTR by default on open, which triggers the firmware to re-emit a SESSION
53	    record. CDC ACM ignores baud rate; we still pass one because pyserial
54	    requires it.
55	    """
56	
57	    def __init__(
58	        self,
59	        port: str,
60	        *,
61	        baudrate: int = 921600,
62	        chunk_bytes: int = 4096,
63	        read_timeout_s: float = 0.1,
64	    ) -> None:
65	        self.port = port
66	        self.baudrate = baudrate
67	        self.chunk_bytes = chunk_bytes
68	        self.read_timeout_s = read_timeout_s
69	        self._ser: object | None = None
70	
71	    def __enter__(self) -> "SerialSource":
72	        # Imported lazily so file-only workflows do not require pyserial.
73	        import serial  # noqa: WPS433  (intentional lazy import)
74	
75	        self._ser = serial.Serial(
76	            port=self.port,
77	            baudrate=self.baudrate,
78	            timeout=self.read_timeout_s,
79	            dsrdtr=False,
80	        )
81	        # Make DTR explicit — some platforms default it off.
82	        try:
83	            self._ser.dtr = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
84	        except (OSError, AttributeError):
85	            pass
86	        return self
87	
88	    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
89	        if self._ser is not None:
90	            try:
91	                self._ser.close()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
92	            finally:
93	                self._ser = None
94	
95	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
96	        if self._ser is None:
97	            raise RuntimeError("SerialSource must be used as a context manager")
98	        ser = self._ser
99	        while True:
100	            # `read` with timeout returns whatever has arrived (possibly empty
101	            # on timeout). `in_waiting` lets us drain the OS buffer in one go
102	            # when bytes are already queued.
103	            n = max(1, getattr(ser, "in_waiting", 0))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
104	            chunk: bytes = ser.read(min(n, self.chunk_bytes))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
105	            if chunk:
106	                yield chunk
107	
108	
109	# ─── Tee — passthrough source that also records to disk ──────────────────────
110	
111	
112	class TeeSource(AbstractContextManager["TeeSource"]):
113	    """Wrap any byte source so every chunk is also appended to a file.
114	
115	    Used by `marvin-perf live --also-record FILE` so a single live session
116	    yields both inline decode output and a `.bin` capture for later
117	    summarize/replay.
118	    """
119	
120	    def __init__(
121	        self,
122	        upstream: Iterable[bytes] | AbstractContextManager[Iterable[bytes]],
123	        out_path: str | Path,
124	    ) -> None:
125	        self.upstream = upstream
126	        self.out_path = Path(out_path)
127	        self._fh: BinaryIO | None = None
128	
129	    def __enter__(self) -> "TeeSource":
130	        self._fh = self.out_path.open("wb")
131	        if isinstance(self.upstream, AbstractContextManager):
132	            self.upstream.__enter__()
133	        return self
134	
135	    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None:
136	        try:
137	            if isinstance(self.upstream, AbstractContextManager):
138	                self.upstream.__exit__(exc_type, exc, tb)
139	        finally:
140	            if self._fh is not None:
141	                self._fh.close()
142	                self._fh = None
143	
144	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
145	        if self._fh is None:
146	            raise RuntimeError("TeeSource must be used as a context manager")
147	        for chunk in self.upstream:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
148	            self._fh.write(chunk)
149	            self._fh.flush()
150	            yield chunk

178	/* ─── Public sink interface ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
179	
180	void PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize(void)
181	{
182	    s_write_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_write_done_buf);
183	    configASSERT(s_write_done != NULL);
184	
185	    /* Open may fail until USB_DEVICE_Initialize finishes its own first
186	     * task tick — retry until success. Drain task is alive at this
187	     * point so vTaskDelay is fine. */
188	    while (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
189	    {
190	        s_dev_handle = USB_DEVICE_Open(USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0,
191	                                       DRV_IO_INTENT_READWRITE);
192	        if (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
193	        {
194	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SINK_OPEN_RETRY_MS));
195	        }
196	    }
197	
198	    USB_DEVICE_EventHandlerSet(s_dev_handle, device_event_handler, 0u);
199	
200	    /* Cold-boot-with-cable case: by the time we register the handler the
201	     * UDPHS driver may have already raced past the VBUS edge it needed
202	     * to fire POWER_DETECTED, or the host may have seen a brief pull-up
203	     * assertion during early boot and given up retrying. Force a clean
204	     * detach→short delay→attach edge so the host sees an unambiguous
205	     * device-arrival on the bus. Hot-plug after this point is unaffected
206	     * because POWER_REMOVED/POWER_DETECTED still drive Detach/Attach. */
207	    (void)USB_DEVICE_Detach(s_dev_handle);
208	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100));
209	    (void)USB_DEVICE_Attach(s_dev_handle);
210	
211	    LOG_INFO("PERF: USB device opened, waiting for host enumeration\r\n");
212	}
213	
214	bool PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected(void)
215	{
216	    return s_is_configured && s_cls.dtr;
217	}
218	
219	void PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(const void *payload, uint16_t len)
220	{
221	    if (!s_is_configured || !s_cls.dtr)
222	    {
223	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
224	        return;

Looking at [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/cli.py:147-165](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/cli.py#L147-L165), the doubling pattern isn't really "two ~1Hz clocks drifting" — it's a structural property of how the host prints `[status]`.

The host loop only checks the timer **when a record arrives**:

```python
for rec in records:
    print(_format_record(rec, ...))
    now = time.monotonic()
    if (now - last_status) >= 1.0:
        print(...)
        last_status = now    # ← anchored to record arrival, not wall grid
```

Two consequences:

1. **Status cadence is anchored to record arrivals, not a free-running 1 s grid.** Each time `[status]` prints, `last_status` snaps to the wall-arrival of the DROP that triggered it. So the host's "1 Hz clock" is effectively `device_period` + skew, not 1.000 s.

2. **The `>= 1.0` test is one-sided.** A DROP whose elapsed-since-last-print is 0.999 s skips the status entirely. The next DROP then sees ~1.998 s elapsed and prints — giving you a "double". With device emitting at very nearly 1 Hz, any sub-millisecond noise on either side (USB-CDC bulk-in coalescing in macOS, FreeRTOS drain-task iteration jitter, scheduler latency on the host) puts arrivals on either side of the threshold roughly evenly, so doubles aren't rare — they're expected fairly often.

It's also worth noting the firmware side at [perf_log.c:149-153](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c#L149-L153) uses the same `>=` pattern with a 20 ms drain-iteration tail, so the device's actual DROP period averages ~1.005-1.020 s, with up-to-20 ms jitter per emission — well into the range that lands on either side of the host's 1.0 s cliff.

**So your gut is right: it's not "slightly out of sync" — it's that the host prints status on a record-anchored, edge-triggered timer with a hard 1.0 s threshold, which makes occasional skip-and-double the *normal* steady state, not a sync artifact.**

If you want a clean 1-per-record cadence, the easiest fix is a free-running grid in `_live_loop`:

```python
next_status = time.monotonic() + 1.0
for rec in records:
    print(_format_record(rec, ...))
    now = time.monotonic()
    if now >= next_status:
        print(...)
        next_status += 1.0  # ← absolute grid, doesn't drift with arrivals
        if now - next_status > 1.0:
            next_status = now + 1.0  # resync if we stalled
```

That decouples status from record arrival jitter so each `[status]` lines up with one DROP except in genuine skew/stall cases.
